data.narrative:
Occam is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Ana Montero Horas and Andre Marques-Smith that has raised $14M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of the three triangulation methods evaluated, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. This method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $35M. Peer-median analysis could not be executed due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow peer set—while 7 same-sector peers exist, none met the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring is not viable in the absence of disclosed revenue figures, which are rarely available for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $30M to $40M, with a median point of $35M. However, the reliance on a single applicable method introduces material uncertainty. Validation would materially strengthen with either (1) revenue disclosure enabling public-comp P/S anchoring against the 9.2x sector median, or (2) identification of additional seed-stage biotech peers with disclosed valuation data. Key risks include stage-multiplier applicability and potential misalignment between historical step-up patterns and current market conditions.
